The bug is in the deepest overloads of the marker removal methods in `CategoryPlot` and `XYPlot`.

Evidence:
- In [CategoryPlot]( /abs/path/org/jfree/chart/plot/CategoryPlot.java:2155 ) `removeDomainMarker(int, Marker, Layer, boolean)` and [CategoryPlot]( /abs/path/org/jfree/chart/plot/CategoryPlot.java:2434 ) `removeRangeMarker(int, Marker, Layer, boolean)`, the code reads a marker list from `foreground...Markers` or `background...Markers` and immediately does `markers.remove(marker)`.
- In [XYPlot]( /abs/path/org/jfree/chart/plot/XYPlot.java:2282 ) `removeDomainMarker(int, Marker, Layer, boolean)` and [XYPlot]( /abs/path/org/jfree/chart/plot/XYPlot.java:2515 ) `removeRangeMarker(int, Marker, Layer, boolean)`, the same pattern exists.
- For a freshly constructed plot, those maps are initialized, but there is no entry for the requested index/layer unless markers were previously added. That means `map.get(new Integer(index))` returns `null`, and `null.remove(...)` throws the `NullPointerException` seen in the tests.

Expected behavior:
- Removing a marker that was never added should return `false`, not throw.

Root cause:
- Missing null check after looking up the marker list from the map.

The fix should be to return `false` when the retrieved `markers` list is `null` before attempting `remove(marker)`.
